satisfactionSources.name: Confirmed understanding
satisfactionSources.rationale: A real experiment confirmed new information; repeated facts do not qualify.

satisfactionSources.name: Participating in an evidence exchange
satisfactionSources.rationale: Separate offer and acceptance around an actual finding; no relation or physical agreement is invented.

capabilityIndex.function: Travel toward a self-chosen coordinate or known object/item using observed obstacles.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: Actual distance times 2, increased by carried mass; speed 0.8 per simulation time unit.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Continues until within the target interaction area or a real failure. Empty target uses x/y. A resource:ID target selects only a remembered ground stack.

capabilityIndex.function: Recover available physical energy at the current position.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Base recovery 4, modified by actually accessible registered facilities; capped at 40.

capabilityIndex.function: Allow one simulation round to pass at the current position.
Transfer a nearby ground stack into personal inventory.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Requires actual distance within pickup reach; resource:ID means a matching nearby visible ground stack.
Actual nutrition and toxicity apply. Food never directly heals. resource:ID selects an owned stack.

capabilityIndex.function: Collect exposed ripe food or loose material from a nearby natural source.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: 2 energy per unit, finite current source stock.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Transfers real source stock to inventory; requires the source interaction range. No processing or felling is implied.

capabilityIndex.function: Place owned units on the ground.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Other actors may subsequently collect the ground stack.

capabilityIndex.function: Hand owned units to an adjacent actor.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Actual recipient identity and distance required; no relationship or happiness is inferred.

capabilityIndex.function: Send a short message to a currently visible actor.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Delivered after the round barrier; recipient text is data, not authority.

capabilityIndex.function: Study an already implemented ability with its declared prerequisites.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: The interface-specific number of simulation rounds.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Implementation does not grant mastery. Already mastered interfaces are reused without new rewards.

capabilityIndex.function: Describe an encountered problem, desired effect and known conditions for functional review.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: A game round to begin study after review; implementation time does not advance simulation.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: World review reuses equivalents or returns a structured development request. No request, learning or descriptive reward. Unknown methods and costs are allowed; the reviewer supplies a minimal feasible specification.

capabilityIndex.function: Observe a nearby subject or physically test a small owned material sample.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

capabilityIndex.function: Read a current-world capability contract or retained personal record.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

capabilityIndex.function: Offer a personally tested finding or independently accept an actual nearby offer.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

capabilityIndex.function: Report personal findings, read shared records or independently respond at the group meeting location.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round and 0.2 energy. Actual local presence is required.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Dated information or a voluntary response only; no free goods, mastery or reward.

capabilityIndex.function: Offer a personally mastered ability to a nearby participant, or accept an actual offer before individual study.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round and 0.2 energy. Actual local presence is required.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Dated information or a voluntary response only; no free goods, mastery or reward.

catalogue.detailAccess: All entries belong to this experiment. Use consult ability with its ID to retain its full executable schema for subsequent decisions. Public implementation does not grant personal mastery.

request.name: Prepare a substantial root meal
request.function: Provide a reusable way to prepare available safe roots into a substantial meal, with actual processing and intake tracked separately where necessary.
request.conditions: I carry three roots. Eating one raw root supplied 14 nutrition with no known toxicity. I am outdoors on ordinary forest soil; no cooking equipment, fuel or heat source has been established.
request.inputs: Available roots; any additional materials or equipment must be explicitly identified and acquired. Method unknown.
request.costs: Unknown; specify feasible material, energy and time costs and any safety prerequisites.
request.effects: Actual prepared food suitable for later consumption, with only physically supported nutrition, safety and meal-experience effects; no assumed benefit merely from naming or learning the method.

shown.question: What feasible preparation can turn available roots into a substantial prepared meal?
evidence: A root eaten at tick 7 provided 14 nutrition.
Three roots remain in my inventory.
No cooking equipment or fuel has been established.
shown.uncertainty: Preparation methods, equipment, material requirements and benefits are unknown.
shown.goal: Discover a feasible, safe method for preparing available food.
shown.missing: A reviewed preparation method and its actual prerequisites.
shown.benefit: Safe raw roots currently provide a food reserve; preparation benefits remain untested.

request.name: Preserve gathered food
request.function: Provide a practical way to slow spoilage of gathered edible roots while keeping them safe to eat.
request.conditions: I am outdoors on ordinary forest soil, healthy, carrying two roots with recorded decay. Nearby root plants are finite food sources. No preservation equipment or method is known to me.
request.inputs: Owned roots; other necessary materials and equipment are unknown and must be obtained if required.
request.costs: Unknown; specify actual work, energy, materials and any ongoing maintenance.
request.effects: Physically reduce food spoilage through a feasible process, report its limits and safety conditions, and retain the food's actual nutritional properties.

shown.description: Arrived after traveling 0.100 distance; spent 0.200 energy.

input.contextPolicy: Object IDs refer to deduplicated actual applicant observations. Whole records are selected with omission counts. Missing detail is unknown, not proof of absence. Full retained state is available during the development handoff; implementation must validate actual prerequisites and ownership.
input.implementation: New interfaces, state, geometry, persistent processes, rendering components and personal memory/task adapters can be delivered through a versioned current-conversation handoff. Source validation and history must remain intact. Declared implementation does not supply stock, objects or mastery.

response.text:
{
  "reviews": [
    {
      "actor": "birch-5",
      "decision": "develop",
      "ability": null,
      "reason": "Eating already handles intake, but no implemented capability prepares food for later consumption. A minimal feasible preparation is crushing safe roots using an acquired stone and bark work surface. It requires no assumed fire, equipment or new food stock. Preparation preserves nutrition rather than creating additional nutrition or detoxification.",
      "specification": "Implement root-preparation-v1. Public schema: {operation:'prepare', inputStackId, quantity, stoneId, barkId, processId?}; use shared actor/item/object/process references, world coordinates, mass units and simulation rounds. Require living actor, individual mastery, positive integral quantity, owned unspoiled meadow roots, an actual owned stone unit and bark unit, and placement on accessible, unoccupied ground within 0.65 interaction distance. Stone and bark are reusable implements, unavailable for simultaneous conflicting operations; acquire them separately. No fire or water is required. Record input identities, quantity, accumulated spoilage, composition, harvest history, tool references, owner, location, remaining work and paid energy. Perform two active rounds per root at 1 energy per round, including setup and crushing. Reserve roots in uniquely owned process escrow; continue their actual decay. Each paid round reduces remaining work exactly once. Pause on movement out of reach or insufficient energy. Completion atomically converts escrow into crushed-root food owned by the actor; conserve edible mass, 14 nutrition per input root, zero initial toxicity, and original provenance. No washing, sterilization or extended shelf life is implied; crushed food decays at 1.25 times its corresponding unprocessed rate and never resets accumulated spoilage. Existing eat must accept this composition and apply normal satiety, toxicity and spoilage rules, without direct healing. Cancellation, including death, releases the actual unfinished crushed/raw mixture at the process location with its current composition and decay; spent effort is not refunded, and escrow is neither duplicated nor deleted. Tools remain actual world items. The work patch is a non-solid radius-0.3 ground footprint, cannot overlap incompatible occupied work surfaces, and creates no room, shade or collision barrier. Declare food-preparation-started and food-preparation-completed; bind paid updates and cancellation to process-progress, process-completed and process-stopped. Dependencies are item reservation, composite edible state, existing decay/eat and shared geometry; implement these in this handoff. Migrate existing stacks unchanged; add processing history only to transformed portions. Keep implementation, individual study and actual execution separate.",
      "experienceReview": "Crushing alone does not earn wellbeing, and there is no established physical reason for a nutrition bonus. Actual eating can provide bounded enjoyment of a substantial safe meal, including repeated enjoyment. Bind one canonical food-enjoyment rule to meal-experience, shared with raw and preserved food rather than a preparation-specific alias: participant is the actual eater; require at least 8 nutrition actually accepted within the existing 10-round meal window, nonspoiled nontoxic food, and a positive appetite at intake. Award 0.4 transient pleasure, source cap 0.8, duration 4 rounds, refresh rather than stack, cooldown 10 rounds per eater across all food forms. Emit at most once for the same intake window; no reward for discarded overflow or processing. This finite meal does not establish a maintained satisfaction source. A separately performed qualifying experiment may use the existing information-confirmed rule through probe, never an automatic reward for completing preparation.",
      "visualReview": "Show the real stone, bark surface and reserved roots at the work location, followed by a visibly crushed food stack only after completion. Display remaining work, paid energy, original ingredients, nutrition, spoilage and the absence of cooking or preservation. Replay paid crushing steps and completion/cancellation using the declared process events; no meal, warmth or wellbeing animation occurs merely on registration or learning.",
      "learning": 2
    },
    {
      "actor": "cedar-6",
      "decision": "develop",
      "ability": null,
      "reason": "No existing function slows spoilage. A small air-drying tray for crushed safe roots is a feasible precursor that requires actual materials and suitable weather. Its effectiveness must depend on measured moisture and exposure, not a preservation label. The two carried roots remain ordinary roots until processing actually occurs.",
      "specification": "Implement root-air-drying-v1. Public schema: {operation:'build'|'load'|'unload'|'dismantle', processId?, trayId?, inputStackId?, quantity?, stoneIds?, barkId?, x?, y?}. Use the same shared reference, coordinate, mass and process contracts as root preparation. Independently implement drying; record reuse of its crushing, food-provenance and escrow code as code reuse, not functional equivalence or personal mastery. Build requires two actual stone units and one bark unit, accessible ground and a living trained actor. Reserve these materials; two active rounds at 1 energy each assemble a non-solid radius-0.4 tray, capacity two root units, with 0.65 interaction reach. Validate shared placement against obstacles and incompatible work footprints. Materials remain conserved components and cannot simultaneously serve another process. Loading requires owned unspoiled meadow roots; crush on the tray using a support stone for two active rounds per root at 1 energy per round. Record all original food composition, harvest and decay history. Root wet mass starts from its actual resource composition: water 50%, other mass 50%; nutrition remains 14 per original root, toxicity zero. After loading, drying is passive, with explicit remaining water-removal work. At each dt=1, when uncovered, not raining and temperature is between 10 and 40 C, remove at most 0.005 mass units of water per root and never below a water fraction of 0.12; transfer removed water to the environmental water ledger. At other temperatures pause drying. Rain adds actual environmental water at up to 0.01 mass per root per round, bounded by the original 50% water fraction. Resolve temperature, rain, cover and exposure from shared weather and geometry, not applicant labels; add a conservative explicit weather-state field if necessary rather than assume favorable conditions. Before dry completion, use crushed-food decay at 1.25 times baseline; at water fraction <=0.12 use 0.35 times baseline while actually dry. Rewetting above 0.12 immediately removes that benefit. Never reset accumulated spoilage, reverse spoiled food, remove toxins or increase nutrients. Completion emits a dried composite food stack retained in the tray; unload transfers that actual stack to inventory. Away from the tray, continue tracking moisture, rain exposure, decay and provenance; no automatic waterproof container. Existing eat consumes its real composition. Owner, component identities, escrow, work progress, moisture, environmental transfers and decay persist. Pause active work on lost reach or energy. Any multi-round actor operation cancels on death, leaving uniquely owned materials and the actual partly processed food at the tray; passive exposure remains physical state, not a dead actor's continuing action. Manual cancellation follows the same rule, without refunds or duplication. Dismantling takes one round and 1 energy, returns actual components at their current condition and deposits any food unchanged. Declare drying-tray-built, food-drying-progress, food-drying-completed and food-rewetted, plus process-progress/process-completed/process-stopped for active work. Dependencies include shared weather/geometry, food water-mass accounting, decay, eat and process ownership; implement within this handoff. Existing foods retain their original decay history; migrate root water composition without changing mass or nutrition. No stock, tray or mastery is supplied by development.",
      "experienceReview": "A completed tray or drying label is not itself pleasure or sustained satisfaction. The measurable benefit is slower subsequent decay while the food remains sufficiently dry. Actual consumption may receive the same canonical meal-experience food-enjoyment rule specified for preparation: actual eater, at least 8 accepted nutrition in a 10-round window, safe nonspoiled intake and positive appetite; 0.4 pleasure, cap 0.8, duration 4, refresh only, 10-round shared food cooldown and one grant per intake window. It is not an additional preserved-food reward. No maintained satisfaction is inferred from unattended storage. A real comparison establishing previously unconfirmed spoilage behavior can qualify through probe and the existing information-confirmed source, subject to that source's novelty, cap and cooldown rules.",
      "visualReview": "Render the acquired stones and bark as a small ground tray with only the food actually loaded. Show paid setup/crushing progress, moisture, drying or rain-paused status, accumulated spoilage and current decay multiplier. Bind shrinking food mass and rewetting to food-drying-progress and food-rewetted; completion changes appearance only when the moisture threshold is reached. Replay water transfers and actual material placement, and clearly distinguish predicted drying work from completed preserved food.",
      "learning": 4
    }
  ]
}

Public schema: {operation:'prepare', inputStackId, quantity, stoneId, barkId, processId?}; use shared actor/item/object/process references, world coordinates, mass units and simulation rounds. Require living actor, individual mastery, positive integral quantity, owned unspoiled meadow roots, an actual owned stone unit and bark unit, and placement on accessible, unoccupied ground within 0.65 interaction distance. Stone and bark are reusable implements, unavailable for simultaneous conflicting operations; acquire them separately. No fire or water is required. Record input identities, quantity, accumulated spoilage, composition, harvest history, tool references, owner, location, remaining work and paid energy. Perform two active rounds per root at 1 energy per round, including setup and crushing. Reserve roots in uniquely owned process escrow; continue their actual decay. Each paid round reduces remaining work exactly once. Pause on movement out of reach or insufficient energy. Completion atomically converts escrow into crushed-root food owned by the actor; conserve edible mass, 14 nutrition per input root, zero initial toxicity, and original provenance. No washing, sterilization or extended shelf life is implied; crushed food decays at 1.25 times its corresponding unprocessed rate and never resets accumulated spoilage. Existing eat must accept this composition and apply normal satiety, toxicity and spoilage rules, without direct healing. Cancellation, including death, releases the actual unfinished crushed/raw mixture at the process location with its current composition and decay; spent effort is not refunded, and escrow is neither duplicated nor deleted. Tools remain actual world items. The work patch is a non-solid radius-0.3 ground footprint, cannot overlap incompatible occupied work surfaces, and creates no room, shade or collision barrier. Declare food-preparation-started and food-preparation-completed; bind paid updates and cancellation to process-progress, process-completed and process-stopped. Dependencies are item reservation, composite edible state, existing decay/eat and shared geometry; implement these in this handoff. Migrate existing stacks unchanged; add processing history only to transformed portions. Keep implementation, individual study and actual execution separate.\",\n      \"experienceReview\": \"Crushing alone does not earn wellbeing, and there is no established physical reason for a nutrition bonus. Actual eating can provide bounded enjoyment of a substantial safe meal, including repeated enjoyment. Bind one canonical food-enjoyment rule to meal-experience, shared with raw and preserved food rather than a preparation-specific alias: participant is the actual eater; require at least 8 nutrition actually accepted within the existing 10-round meal window, nonspoiled nontoxic food, and a positive appetite at intake. Award 0.4 transient pleasure, source cap 0.8, duration 4 rounds, refresh rather than stack, cooldown 10 rounds per eater across all food forms. Emit at most once for the same intake window; no reward for discarded overflow or processing. This finite meal does not establish a maintained satisfaction source. A separately performed qualifying experiment may use the existing information-confirmed rule through probe, never an automatic reward for completing preparation.\",\n      \"visualReview\": \"Show the real stone, bark surface and reserved roots at the work location, followed by a visibly crushed food stack only after completion. Display remaining work, paid energy, original ingredients, nutrition, spoilage and the absence of cooking or preservation. Replay paid crushing steps and completion/cancellation using the declared process events; no meal, warmth or wellbeing animation occurs merely on registration or learning.\",\n      \"learning\": 2\n    },\n    {\n      \"actor\": \"cedar-6\",\n      \"decision\": \"develop\",\n      \"ability\": null,\n      \"reason\": \"No existing function slows spoilage. A small air-drying tray for crushed safe roots is a feasible precursor that requires actual materials and suitable weather. Its effectiveness must depend on measured moisture and exposure, not a preservation label. The two carried roots remain ordinary roots until processing actually occurs.\",\n      \"specification\": \"Implement root-air-drying-v1. Public schema: {operation:'build'|'load'|'unload'|'dismantle', processId?, trayId?, inputStackId?, quantity?, stoneIds?, barkId?, x?, y?}. Use the same shared reference, coordinate, mass and process contracts as root preparation. Independently implement drying; record reuse of its crushing, food-provenance and escrow code as code reuse, not functional equivalence or personal mastery. Build requires two actual stone units and one bark unit, accessible ground and a living trained actor. Reserve these materials; two active rounds at 1 energy each assemble a non-solid radius-0.4 tray, capacity two root units, with 0.65 interaction reach. Validate shared placement against obstacles and incompatible work footprints. Materials remain conserved components and cannot simultaneously serve another process. Loading requires owned unspoiled meadow roots; crush on the tray using a support stone for two active rounds per root at 1 energy per round. Record all original food composition, harvest and decay history. Root wet mass starts from its actual resource composition: water 50%, other mass 50%; nutrition remains 14 per original root, toxicity zero. After loading, drying is passive, with explicit remaining water-removal work. At each dt=1, when uncovered, not raining and temperature is between 10 and 40 C, remove at most 0.005 mass units of water per root and never below a water fraction of 0.12; transfer removed water to the environmental water ledger. At other temperatures pause drying. Rain adds actual environmental water at up to 0.01 mass per root per round, bounded by the original 50% water fraction. Resolve temperature, rain, cover and exposure from shared weather and geometry, not applicant labels; add a conservative explicit weather-state field if necessary rather than assume favorable conditions. Before dry completion, use crushed-food decay at 1.25 times baseline; at water fraction <=0.12 use 0.35 times baseline while actually dry. Rewetting above 0.12 immediately removes that benefit. Never reset accumulated spoilage, reverse spoiled food, remove toxins or increase nutrients. Completion emits a dried composite food stack retained in the tray; unload transfers that actual stack to inventory. Away from the tray, continue tracking moisture, rain exposure, decay and provenance; no automatic waterproof container. Existing eat consumes its real composition. Owner, component identities, escrow, work progress, moisture, environmental transfers and decay persist. Pause active work on lost reach or energy. Any multi-round actor operation cancels on death, leaving uniquely owned materials and the actual partly processed food at the tray; passive exposure remains physical state, not a dead actor's continuing action. Manual cancellation follows the same rule, without refunds or duplication. Dismantling takes one round and 1 energy, returns actual components at their current condition and deposits any food unchanged. Declare drying-tray-built, food-drying-progress, food-drying-completed and food-rewetted, plus process-progress/process-completed/process-stopped for active work. Dependencies include shared weather/geometry, food water-mass accounting, decay, eat and process ownership; implement within this handoff. Existing foods retain their original decay history; migrate root water composition without changing mass or nutrition. No stock, tray or mastery is supplied by development.\",\n      \"experienceReview\": \"A completed tray or drying label is not itself pleasure or sustained satisfaction. The measurable benefit is slower subsequent decay while the food remains sufficiently dry. Actual consumption may receive the same canonical meal-experience food-enjoyment rule specified for preparation: actual eater, at least 8 accepted nutrition in a 10-round window, safe nonspoiled intake and positive appetite; 0.4 pleasure, cap 0.8, duration 4, refresh only, 10-round shared food cooldown and one grant per intake window. It is not an additional preserved-food reward. No maintained satisfaction is inferred from unattended storage. A real comparison establishing previously unconfirmed spoilage behavior can qualify through probe and the existing information-confirmed source, subject to that source's novelty, cap and cooldown rules.\",\n      \"visualReview\": \"Render the acquired stones and bark as a small ground tray with only the food actually loaded. Show paid setup/crushing progress, moisture, drying or rain-paused status, accumulated spoilage and current decay multiplier. Bind shrinking food mass and rewetting to food-drying-progress and food-rewetted; completion changes appearance only when the moisture threshold is reached. Replay water transfers and actual material placement, and clearly distinguish predicted drying work from completed preserved food.\",\n      \"learning\": 4\n    }\n  ]\n}","logprobs":[]}
